content_zh:
“文王拉车八百步，大周天下八千年。”
“九州之外，妖蛮环伺；九州之内，藩王裂土，背天换骨，是凡人登仙的唯一途径。”
“百步人仙，千步地仙，万步天仙……”
大周历七千九百八十三年。
安阳村一座漏风的破庙里，庙里没有菩萨，只有一块被虫蛀了大半的牌匾，上面写着“安阳学塾”四个字。
说是学塾，其实就是一间荒芜破败，摇摇欲坠的，仅能挡雨的破屋。
此时，一个白发苍苍的老夫子站在正堂前，对着底下十几个面黄肌瘦，十八九岁的少男少女讲得唾沫横飞。
“老夫年轻时，曾亲眼见过一位仙人出手，那是在祁山脚下，一头三百年道行的熊妖一路向南踏平了三个村子，上千口人一夜之间被啃得骨头都不剩，后来一位仙人御剑而来，只出了一掌。”
他伸出枯瘦的手掌，缓缓向前一推。
“隔着一座山头，那熊妖连惨叫都没来得及发出来，便被拍成了一摊肉泥。”
“后来老夫才知，那位仙人不过是最寻常的五骨人仙，在仙门里连内门弟子都算不上。”
底下的十几个少年少女听得眼睛发直，大气都不敢喘。
老夫子很满意这个效果，缓了口气，继续道，“当初老夫当年在洛水边上，见过两位仙人斗法，其中一位一剑斩出去，天上的云都被劈成了两半，整整三天没有合拢，那一剑的光，隔着百里都能看见，比天上的太阳还亮。”
他越说越激动。
“所以你们要记住——只要身怀仙骨，哪怕只有一块，那也是天大的造化！拥有仙骨者，背天而行，每走一步便碎一块凡骨，换一块仙骨，走到百步，便成人仙，可镇守一方王朝千年不灭！”
他顿了顿，浑浊的目光扫过底下每一张稚嫩的脸。
“还有几日，仙门便会来人招收弟子，一旦被仙门选中，从此便鲤鱼跃龙门，再不用在这个破地方担惊受怕，你们的爹娘也能跟着享福，明白了吗？”
“明白！”十几个少年少女齐声应道。
唯独有一个声音慢了半拍。
老夫子皱了皱眉，目光越过前排几个脑袋，落在学塾最后面靠墙的位置。

那里坐着一个十八九岁的少年，穿着一身洗得发白的灰布衣裳，袖口磨出了毛边，脸上没什么肉，但一双眼睛很干净。
此刻他正微微侧着头，像是在认真听讲，又像是什么都没在听。
“林罪！”
老夫子提高声音。
少年眨了眨眼，慢吞吞地站起来，“夫子。”
“可记住了否？”
“记住了。”
林罪回答得很干脆，但老夫子总觉得林罪态度敷衍，哼了一声，“那你给老夫说说，百步是什么仙？”
“百步人仙。”
“千步呢？”
“千步地仙。”
“万步？”
“万步天仙。”
content_en:
"King Wen pulled his chariot eight hundred paces, and the Great Zhou Dynasty lasted eight thousand years."
"Beyond the Nine Provinces, demons and barbarians are around; within the Nine Provinces, the vassal kings split the earth and change their bones. This is the only way for mortals to become immortals."
"A hundred-step human immortal, a thousand-step earth immortal, a thousand-step heavenly immortal..."
Seven thousand nine hundred and eighty-three years of the Great Zhou Calendar.
In a leaky and dilapidated temple in Anyang Village, there is no Bodhisattva in the temple. There is only a plaque that is mostly eaten by insects, with the words "Anyang School" written on it.
It was said to be a school, but in fact it was a deserted, dilapidated, crumbling house that could only keep out the rain.
At this time, a gray-haired old master stood in front of the main hall, talking to a dozen sallow and thin boys and girls below him.
"When I was young, I saw an immortal attack with my own eyes. It was at the foot of Qi Mountain. A bear demon with three hundred years of Taoism trampled three villages all the way south. Thousands of people were chewed up to the bone overnight. Then an immortal came with a sword and only struck out one palm."
He stretched out his skinny palm and pushed forward slowly.
"Across a mountain, the bear demon didn't even have time to scream, before he was beaten into a pile of meat."
"Later I found out that the immortal was just the most ordinary Five Bones Immortal, and he was not even considered an inner disciple in the Immortal Sect."
The dozen or so boys and girls below heard this with their eyes straightened, and they didn't dare to breathe.
The old master was very satisfied with the effect. He took a breath and continued, "Back then, I saw two immortals fighting on the edge of Luoshui River. One of them slashed out with a sword, and the clouds in the sky were split in half. They did not close up for three days. The light of that sword could be seen a hundred miles away, and it was brighter than the sun in the sky."
The more he spoke, the more excited he became.
"So you must remember - as long as you have an immortal bone, even if you only have one, it is a great blessing! Those who have immortal bones will walk with their backs to the sky. Every step they take will break a mortal bone and replace it with another immortal bone. After walking a hundred steps, they will become an immortal and can guard a dynasty for thousands of years!"
He paused, his turbid eyes scanning every young face underneath.
"In a few days, the Immortal Sect will come to recruit disciples. Once chosen by the Immortal Sect, they will leap over the Dragon Gate from now on. You no longer have to worry about this poor place, and your parents can also enjoy the blessings. Do you understand?"
"Understood!" More than a dozen boys and girls responded in unison.
Only one voice was half a beat slow.
The old master frowned, looking past the heads in the front row and landing on the wall at the back of the school.
Sitting there was a boy of eighteen or nineteen years old, wearing a suit of gray cloth that had been washed white, with rough edges on the cuffs. There was no flesh on his face, but his eyes were very clean.
At this moment, he was tilting his head slightly, as if he was listening carefully, but also as if he was not listening to anything.
"Lin Sin!"
The old master raised his voice.
The young man blinked and stood up slowly, "Master."
"Do you remember it?"
"Remember."
Lin Zui answered very simply, but the old master always felt that Lin Zui's attitude was perfunctory, so he snorted, "Then tell me, what kind of immortal is Baibu?"
"A hundred-step human immortal."
"Where's Qianbu?"
"Thousand-Step Earth Immortal."
"Wanbu?"
"Ten Thousand Steps of Heavenly Immortal."
